Hi Kevin,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really appreciate the time. Per our discussion, attaching a short summary and our private/VPC deployment checklist to help guide the next steps.

Quick recap and asks: 
- Goal: Private VPC deployment of Redwood inference for production workloads (PHI/PII scoped).
- High-level topology: customer VPC peering / private link into a customer-managed subnet with traffic restrictions and egress controls.
- Questions we need from your side to qualify:
  1) What categories of PII/PHI will be sent to the model (full SSNs, partial IDs, patient notes, etc.)?
  2) Desired data retention policy for prompts & logs (days/months/never).
  3) Audit/logging expectations (request/response logging, access logs, KMS audit trails).
  4) Any strict egress constraints (no internet egress from the VPC, only to specific endpoints).
  5) On-prem / air-gapped requirements or planned hybrid setup.

Attachments: redwood_private_vpc_requirements.pdf (checklist + diagram stub)

Next steps I propose:
- You share your network diagram and security requirements (diagram + list).
- We'll schedule a technical deep-dive to map dataflow and egress controls (30-45m).
- Align on a mutual action plan and timeline for a Private deployment POC.

If you can share the network diagram and the answers above, we can get the infra/engineering folks looped in.

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Attaching our high-level network diagram and security requirements. Answers inline below: 

On PII: primary payload will be patient clinical notes (PHI), hashed patient IDs, and occasionally partial SSNs (redacted where possible). We treat clinical notes as sensitive and require encryption in transit and at rest.

Data retention: default retention for AI logs is 30 days; for audit logs we retain 7 years per policy, but we are open to shorter retention for model prompts if Redwood supports it.

Logging: we need request/response logging disabled by default for model content. Access logs (who/when) must be retained and forwarded to our SIEM. KMS audit trails are required for key usage.

Egress: NO internet egress from the processing subnet except to our on-prem backup endpoint and the Redundancy/Control plane endpoints that we will whitelist.

On-prem: we do have a locked-down on-prem cluster and may require an air-gapped option for certain workloads. For the POC, we prefer a VPC-to-on-prem private link with no public endpoints.

Attachments: acme_network_diagram.vsdx, acme_security_requirements.xlsx

Kevin
Kevin Ross
Infrastructure Security Lead
AcmeHealth

Kevin — thanks for the quick responses and for sharing the diagrams. This is exactly the level of detail we need to scope a POC. Below I've converted your answers into a short qualification checklist and proposed MA P (mutual action plan).

Qualification summary: 
- Data types: PHI (clinical notes), hashed IDs, occasional partial SSNs — treat as sensitive.
- Retention: preferred model prompt retention = 0-30 days; audit logs = 7 years (we can store metadata-only).
- Logging: request/response content should be disabled/pseudonymized for sensitive flows; access logs routed to your SIEM; KMS audit trails required.
- Egress: no public internet from processing subnet; allow only to whitelisted control-plane endpoints and on-prem backup endpoint.
- On-prem / air-gap: POC via private link to on-prem; longer-term air-gapped option may be needed for regulated flows.

Mutual action plan (proposed):
1) Technical deep-dive (this week): map exact network boundaries, required firewall rules, load balancer config. (Owner: Redwood infra + Acme infra)
2) Data handling policy alignment: finalize retention, redaction, and logging approach for POC. (Owner: Security teams)
3) POC deployment: private link/VPC peering configuration + sample workload and verification tests (latency, egress audit). (Owner: Redwood eng + Acme eng)
4) Security review & sign-off: SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration test, and egress verification. (Owner: Security teams)

Action items for you: please confirm the preferred retention window for model prompts (0 / 7 / 30 days), and confirm the on-prem endpoint FQDN we should allow for POC. Also, let us know any additional compliance docs you need up front (we can share SOC2, penetration test summaries, and our private deployment checklist).

I've attached a redlined version of our suggested retention matrix (redwood-data-retention-policy.xlsx) and a link to a shared drive with our SOC2 summary.

Propose slots for the deep-dive: Tue 12/14 9:00-9:45 PT or Thu 12/16 11:00-11:45 PT. If neither works, provide 2-3 alternatives.

Thanks — looping Priyom to coordinate the POC timeline and engineering resources.
